header.logoTagline: Your ideas, your audience, your blog.

banner.title: Your words deserve a good home.
banner.subtitle: Start a blog in minutes, write alone or with your team, and keep every word you publish.
banner.body: Lexicon is a calm, fast place to write. There are no plugins to install, no themes to fight with and no ads between you and your readers. Create your blog, open the editor and publish your first post today.

writing.title: A calm writing space
writing.body: A clean editor with drafts, autosave and featured images. Everything you need to write, nothing that gets in your way.

team.title: Built for writing together
team.body: Invite authors, editors and reviewers to your blog. A built in review step keeps quality high without endless message threads.

ownership.title: Your words stay yours
ownership.body: Export everything you have written whenever you want. If you ever leave, your content leaves with you.

items.tip1: Start your first blog in 10 minutes. From new account to published post, the short version.

about.title: About
about.body: Lexicon is a new blogging platform built for creators who value simplicity, speed, and creative control. We're just getting started, and you're invited to be part of it. Whether you're writing your first post or launching a new project, Lexicon gives you a clean, flexible way to publish and build your blog at your own pace.

step1.title: Create your account
step1.body: Sign up with your email and name your blog. There is nothing to install and nothing to configure.

step2.title: Write and publish
step2.body: Open the clean editor, add a featured image and hit publish. Your post goes live with its own link you can share anywhere.

step3.title: Grow at your own pace
step3.body: Invite people to write with you, organize posts with categories and tags, and let readers join in through comments.

showcase.subtitle: Posts picked by our editors from writers across Lexicon.
showcase.emptyTitle: New here? Start with these guides

q1.a: Yes. Creating an account and starting a blog costs nothing. Optional paid extras may come later, but writing and publishing will stay free.

q2.a: No. If you can write an email you can publish on Lexicon. You sign up, name your blog and start writing.

q3.q: Can I write with other people?
q3.a: Yes. Invite people by email and give each one a role. Authors publish their own posts, contributors submit drafts, editors manage the whole blog and reviewers approve posts before they go live.

q4.a: You do. You can export a full copy of your writing at any time from your dashboard, and deleting your account removes your personal data from the platform.

q5.q: Can readers comment on my posts?
q5.a: Yes, and you stay in charge. Comments can be switched on or off per blog or per post, and you decide what appears under your writing.

q6.q: Can I use my own domain?
q6.a: Not yet. Custom domains are on the roadmap. For now every blog gets its own clean address on Lexicon.

about.title: What is counted
about.counted: A view is a page of this blog opened by a reader. Crawlers, link previews and browsers that ask not to be tracked are left out.

pages.overview: The headline numbers of the other pages. Each block links to the page with the full list.
pages.content: Posts are ranked by views in the range. Their shape compares the first week with the months after.
pages.audience: Countries come from the reader's network address, looked up and then forgotten. Languages are the language of the page read.
pages.acquisition: Each view keeps how its reader arrived. Landing pages are where readers started a visit from outside; exit pages are where they last were.
pages.engagement: A visit is one reader with less than 30 minutes between pages. It is engaged with two or more pages, 10 or more seconds of reading, or a like, comment, save, share or sign-up.
pages.goals: Goals are counted when they happen, and kept after the views are gone. Rates per visit start on the first day visits were counted.

pages.technical: Missing pages are kept for 30 days, because their addresses come from strangers.
pages.post: Everything about one post: its readers, where they came from, and how it did since it was published.
